title: compact-oncall-checklist-and-ephemeral-log-grabber
author: Ravi Menon
release_notes: Add compact on-call checklist UI in the console and an ephemeral log grabber CLI for safe short-lived telemetry snapshots.
description:
Context and motivation: Our on-call console currently surfaces long-form runbooks and full trace links which are useful but slow down triage in noisy alerts. Pager responders repeatedly told us they want a \"one-line action checklist\" they can scan and action in <30s plus a lightweight way to grab the minimal logs/metrics needed for a fast postmortem. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a compact checklist panel (UI + API) that renders prioritized remediation steps with status buttons and links, and 2) an ephemeral log-grabber CLI that collects filtered logs, recent spans, and a minimal metrics snapshot with automatic sanitization and TTL deletion.

Summary of changes and commits: Commit 1 - api: add /v1/oncall/compact-checklist endpoint and checklist schema (includes priorities and action-ids). Commit 2 - ui: compact checklist panel, keyboard shortcuts, and per-action telemetry hooks. Commit 3 - cli: ephemeral-log-grabber tool with kube/logstore adapters and sanitizers. Commit 4 - e2e: tests for checklist state transitions and CLI collection + TTL expiry simulation. Commit 5 - docs: oncall quickstart and CLI usage examples.

Files touched (high level): src/ui/oncall/compactChecklist.tsx, src/api/oncall/checklistHandler.go, tools/ephemeral-log-grabber/main.go, internal/logsanitizer/sanitize.go, test/e2e/oncall_compact_checklist.test.ts, docs/oncall/quickstart_compact_checklist.md.

Behavioral notes: Checklist items support three states (todo, in-progress, done) and emit a short event to the telemetry ingestion pipeline. The CLI uploads a short manifest to the secure artifact store and returns a one-time URL valid for the configured TTL (default 1 hour). All log captures run through sanitize.go which strips PII patterns and token-looking strings by default; customers can opt-out of capture of environment variables in private deployments via a feature flag (off by default).
security_and_compliance: The log-grabber enforces RBAC checks in the API and requires the oncall role in the private control plane. CLI auth uses the existing service token flow; the upload is encrypted server-side and marked ephemeral with automatic garbage collection. A security review was performed (notes in ENG-4321) and we added a telemetry privacy toggle per-customer.
testing_and_ci: Unit tests for sanitizer heuristics and checklist state machine added (coverage +6%). E2E tests simulate an alert, exercise the checklist transitions and CLI collection, and assert that uploaded bundles expire after TTL. CI: lint/pass on first run, flaky e2e re-run once; final status: pass.
review_conversation: Clara: "Can we make the TTL configurable per-org and ensure the default is conservative?" Author: "Yes — added org-level override in the API and documented default=1h." Diego: "Sanitizer heuristics look aggressive; add a fallback review step if a capture triggers too many redactions." Author: "Added a dry-run mode that produces a redaction report and blocks upload when >80% of the bundle is redacted (configurable)." Evan: "UI looks tight; consider keyboard-first flow for pagers." Author: "Added keyboard mapping (c to open checklist, r to start a capture)." QA: "Found a race when rapidly toggling checklist states." Author: "Fixed with optimistic updates + server-side reconciliation; added regression test."
performance_and_operational_impact: Checklist panel lazy-loads to avoid impacting alert rendering. The CLI grabs are intentionally rate-limited and sized (default max 10MB) to keep storage costs bounded; the artifact store enforces per-org quota and GC policies, surfaced in the console. No change to existing alert delivery path.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated (on by default for internal orgs, off for customers until opt-in). Gradual rollout: 10% of orgs for 48 hours, expand to 50% after telemetry confirms no spike in artifact volume, then full rollout. We added alerts to monitor artifact error rates and sanitizer rejection rates.
related_work_and_docs: ENG-4321 tracks follow-ups (searchable snapshot retention UX, per-action runbook attachments). Docs added to docs/oncall/quickstart_compact_checklist.md and CLI usage in docs/tools/ephemeral-log-grabber.md.
merge_outcome: Squash merged to main after approvals from Clara and Diego and CI green. Follow-ups: add server-side retention UI and a per-action edit flow (ENG-4321).
